translations.literal: The Princess of Jiashan, mother Consort Wang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Jiashan, daughter of Consort Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 成化二年下嫁王增，兵部尚書驥孫也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua she married Wang Zeng, grandson of the Minister of War Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 2 she married Wang Zeng, grandson of Minister of War Ji.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Hongzhi year 12.

sentences.zh: 淳安公主，成化二年下嫁蔡震。

translations.literal: The Princess of Chun'an, in the second year of Chenghua married Cai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Chun'an married Cai Zhen in Chenghua year 2.

sentences.zh: 震行醇謹。

translations.literal: Zhen's conduct was pure and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was upright and discreet in conduct.

sentences.zh: 正德中，劉瑾下獄，詔廷訊。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign Liu Jin was imprisoned; an edict ordered trial at court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign Liu Jin was imprisoned and the court ordered a public interrogation.

sentences.zh: 有問者，瑾輒指其人附己，廷臣無敢詰。

translations.literal: When questioned, Jin would point at someone as having joined him; court ministers did not dare press further.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever questioned, Jin would point at someone and claim him as an accomplice, and the ministers at court dared not press further.

sentences.zh: 震歷聲曰：「我皇家至戚，應不附爾！」

translations.literal: Zhen raised his voice and said: "I am the imperial clan's closest kin—surely I would not join you!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen spoke up loudly: "I am the emperor's closest kin by marriage—I would never have joined you!"

sentences.zh: 趣獄卒考掠之，瑾乃服罪，以是知名。

translations.literal: He urged the prison guards to torture him; Jin then confessed guilt, and by this became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the guards to torture him instead. Jin then confessed, and Zhen became famous for this act.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中卒，贈太保，謚康僖。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian and posthumous title Healthy and Gracious.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Jiajing reign and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian with the temple name Healthy and Gracious.

sentences.zh: 崇德公主，母楊安妃。

translations.literal: The Princess of Chongde, mother Consort Yang An.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Chongde, daughter of Consort Yang An.

sentences.zh: 成化二年下嫁楊偉，興濟伯善孫也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua she married Yang Wei, grandson of Marquis Shan of Xingji.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 2 she married Yang Wei, grandson of Marquis Shan of Xingji.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Hongzhi year 2.

sentences.zh: 廣德公主，母萬宸妃。

translations.literal: The Princess of Guangde, mother Consort Wan Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Guangde, daughter of Consort Wan Chen.

sentences.zh: 成化八年下嫁樊凱。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua she married Fan Kai.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 8 she married Fan Kai.

sentences.zh: 二十年八月薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twentieth year she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eighth month of year 20.

sentences.zh: 宜興公主，母魏德妃。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yixing, mother Consort Wei De.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yixing, daughter of Consort Wei De.

sentences.zh: 成化九年下嫁馬誠。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chenghua she married Ma Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 9 she married Ma Cheng.

sentences.zh: 正德九年薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Zhengde year 9.

sentences.zh: 隆慶公主，母高淑妃。

translations.literal: The Princess of Longqing, mother Consort Gao Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Longqing, daughter of Consort Gao Shu.

sentences.zh: 成化九年下嫁遊泰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chenghua she married You Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 9 she married You Tai.

sentences.zh: 十五年薨。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in year 15.

sentences.zh: 嘉祥公主，母妃劉氏。

translations.literal: The Princess of Jiaxiang, mother Consort Lady Liu.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Jiaxiang, daughter of Consort Lady Liu.

sentences.zh: 成化十三年下嫁黃鏞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chenghua she married Huang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 13 she married Huang Yong.

sentences.zh: 後六年薨。

translations.literal: Six years later she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died six years later.

sentences.zh: 景帝一女

translations.literal: One daughter of the Jing Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor's one daughter

sentences.zh: 固安公主，英宗復辟，降稱郡主。

translations.literal: The Princess of Gu'an; when Yingzong was restored to the throne, her title was reduced to Commandery Mistress.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Gu'an. When Yingzong was restored to the throne, her title was reduced to Commandery Mistress.

sentences.zh: 成化時，年已長，憲宗以閣臣奏，五年十一月下嫁王憲。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign she was already advanced in years; Xianzong, on the memorial of grand secretaries, in the eleventh month of the fifth year had her marry Wang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: By the Chenghua reign she was already elderly. On the grand secretaries' recommendation, Xianzong had her marry Wang Xian in the eleventh month of year 5.

sentences.zh: 禮儀視公主，以故尚書蹇義賜第賜之。

translations.literal: Ceremonial observances were as for a princess; the former Minister Jian Yi was granted a residence and it was bestowed on her.
translations.idiomatic: She was accorded the ceremonial honors of a princess, and the former residence of Minister Jian Yi was granted to her.

sentences.zh: 憲宗五女

translations.literal: Five daughters of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong's five daughters

sentences.zh: 仁和公主，弘治二年下嫁齊世美。

translations.literal: The Princess of Renhe, in the second year of Hongzhi married Qi Shimei.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Renhe married Qi Shimei in Hongzhi year 2.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Jiajing year 23.

sentences.zh: 永康公主，弘治六年下嫁崔元。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yongkang, in the sixth year of Hongzhi married Cui Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongkang married Cui Yuan in Hongzhi year 6.

sentences.zh: 元，代州人，世宗入繼，以迎立功封京山侯，給誥券。

translations.literal: Yuan was a man of Daizhou; when Shizong entered the succession, for merit in welcoming him he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingshan and granted a patent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was from Daizhou. When Shizong took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingshan for his service in welcoming the new emperor and granted a patent of appointment.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「奉迎乃臣子之分，遽膺封爵，無故事。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "Welcoming the emperor is a subject's duty; to suddenly receive enfeoffment has no precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites objected: "Welcoming the emperor is merely a subject's duty. There is no precedent for enfeoffment on that account alone."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「永樂初年，太宗入繼大統，駙馬都尉王寧以翊戴功封永春侯，何得言無故事。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the early years of Yongle, when Taizong entered the great succession, Commandant Wang Ning was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchun for supporting the enthronement—how can one say there is no precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "In the early Yongle reign, when Taizong took the throne, Commandant Wang Ning was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchun for supporting his accession. How can you say there is no precedent?"

sentences.zh: 給事中底蘊、御史高越等連章論其不可。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Di Yun, Censor Gao Yue, and others submitted successive memorials arguing it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Di Yun, censor Gao Yue, and others submitted repeated memorials arguing against it.

sentences.zh: 皆不聽。

translations.literal: All were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 已，坐張延齡事下詔獄，尋釋。

translations.literal: Later, on account of the Zhang Yanling affair he was sent to the imperial prison, then soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was imprisoned over the Zhang Yanling affair but was soon released.

sentences.zh: 元好交文士，播聲譽，寵幸優渥，勛臣戚畹莫敢望焉。

translations.literal: Yuan loved to associate with literary men, spread his reputation, enjoyed lavish favor—no meritorious minister or imperial affinal kin dared compare.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan cultivated literary circles, built his reputation, and enjoyed lavish favor at court such that no meritorious minister or imperial in-law dared rival him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十八年卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing year 28.

sentences.zh: 贈左柱國太傅兼太子太傅，謚榮恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Pillar of the State, Grand Tutor, and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Glorious and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Pillar of the State, Grand Tutor, and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the temple name Glorious and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 駙馬封侯贈官不以軍功自元始。

translations.literal: A commandant's enfeoffment as marquis and posthumous offices not based on military merit began with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan onward, commandants were enfeoffed as marquises and granted posthumous offices without military merit.

sentences.zh: 主先元薨。

translations.literal: The princess died before Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The princess died before Yuan.

sentences.zh: 德清公主，弘治九年下嫁林嶽。

translations.literal: The Princess of Deqing, in the ninth year of Hongzhi married Lin Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Deqing married Lin Yue in Hongzhi year 9.

sentences.zh: 嶽字鎮卿，應天人，少習舉子業，奉母孝，撫弟巒極友愛。

translations.literal: Yue, style name Zhenqing, was a man of Yingtian; in youth he studied examination learning, was filial to his mother, and treated his younger brother Luan with utmost brotherly love.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, courtesy name Zhenqing, was from Yingtian. In youth he studied for the civil examinations, was filial to his mother, and treated his younger brother Luan with utmost brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 主亦有賢行，事姑如齊民禮。

translations.literal: The princess also had worthy conduct, serving her mother-in-law with the rites of common households.
translations.idiomatic: The princess also had worthy conduct and served her mother-in-law with the rites of common households.

sentences.zh: 嶽卒於正德十三年，主孀居三十一年始薨。

translations.literal: Yue died in the thirteenth year of Zhengde; the princess remained widowed thirty-one years before she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Yue died in Zhengde year 13. The princess remained widowed for thirty-one years before she died.

sentences.zh: 長泰公主，成化二十三年薨，追冊。

translations.literal: The Princess of Changtai passed away in the twenty-third year of Chenghua and was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Changtai died in Chenghua year 23 and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 仙遊公主，弘治五年薨，追冊。

translations.literal: The Princess of Xianyou passed away in the fifth year of Hongzhi and was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Xianyou died in Hongzhi year 5 and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 孝宗三女

translations.literal: Three daughters of Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong's three daughters

sentences.zh: 太康公主，弘治十一年薨，未下嫁。

translations.literal: The Princess of Taikang passed away in the eleventh year of Hongzhi, not yet married.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Taikang died unmarried in Hongzhi year 11.

sentences.zh: 永福公主，嘉靖二年下嫁鄔景和。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yongfu, in the second year of Jiajing married Wu Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongfu married Wu Jinghe in Jiajing year 2.

sentences.zh: 景和，昆山人，嘗奉旨直西苑，撰玄文，以不諳玄理辭。

translations.literal: Jinghe was a man of Kunshan; he had been ordered to serve duty at the Western Park and compose arcane texts, but declined on grounds of not understanding arcane principles.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe was from Kunshan. He had been ordered to serve at the Western Park and compose arcane texts, but declined on the grounds that he did not understand such doctrines.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 時有事清馥殿，在直諸臣俱行祝厘禮，景和不俟禮成而出。

translations.literal: At the time there was a ceremony at the Qingfu Hall; all ministers on duty performed the blessing rite, but Jinghe left before the rite was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When a blessing ceremony was held at the Qingfu Hall, all ministers on duty performed the rite, but Jinghe left before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 已而賞賚諸臣，景和與焉。

translations.literal: Later rewards were bestowed on the ministers, and Jinghe was included.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were later distributed to the ministers, Jinghe was included.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「無功受賞，懼增罪戾。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Receiving reward without merit, I fear increases guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I have received reward without merit and fear this only deepens my guilt.

sentences.zh: 乞容辭免，俾洗心滌慮，以效他日馬革裹屍、啣環結草之報。」

translations.literal: I beg permission to decline, that I may cleanse heart and thoughts, to repay in future days with death wrapped in horsehide and the knotted-grass debt of gratitude."
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to decline, so that I may purify my heart and thoughts and one day repay Your Majesty with my life on the battlefield and the gratitude owed even from beyond the grave."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謂詛咒失人臣禮，削職歸原籍，時主已薨矣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, saying he had cursed and failed the minister's rites; his office was stripped and he returned to his native place—the princess had already passed away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, declaring that his words amounted to a curse and violated a subject's duty. Jinghe was stripped of office and sent home. The princess had already died.

sentences.zh: 三十五年入賀聖誕畢，因言：「臣自五世祖寄籍錦衣衛，世居北地。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, having finished congratulating the imperial birthday, he said: "From my fifth-generation ancestor my household was registered with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; we have long dwelt in the north.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35, after attending the imperial birthday celebration, he said: "Since my fifth-generation ancestor our household has been registered with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and has long lived in the north.

sentences.zh: 今被罪南徙，不勝犬馬戀主之私。

translations.literal: Now condemned and moved south, I cannot overcome the private longing of dog and horse for their master.
translations.idiomatic: Now condemned and sent south, I cannot overcome my loyal longing for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 扶服入賀，退而私省公主墳墓，丘封翳然，荊棘不剪。

translations.literal: In mourning garb I came to congratulate; afterward I privately visited the princess's tomb—the mound overgrown, brambles uncut.
translations.idiomatic: I came in mourning garb to offer congratulations, then privately visited the princess's tomb. The mound was overgrown and the brambles untrimmed.

sentences.zh: 臣切自念，狐死尚正首丘，臣托命貴主，獨與逝者魂魄相吊於數千里外，不得春秋祭掃，拊心傷悔，五內崩裂。

translations.literal: I deeply reflect: even a fox at death turns its head toward its mound; I entrusted my life to the noble princess, yet alone mourn the departed spirit thousands of li away, unable to perform spring and autumn sacrifices—beating my breast in grief and remorse, my five viscera rent asunder.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect deeply that even a fox turns its head toward its home mound at death. I entrusted my life to the noble princess, yet I mourn her spirit alone thousands of li away, unable to perform the spring and autumn sacrifices. My heart is torn with grief and remorse.

sentences.zh: 臣之罪重，不敢祈恩，惟陛下幸哀故主，使得寄籍原衛，長與相依，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: My guilt is heavy; I dare not beg grace—only that Your Majesty pity my late mistress and permit me to register again with my original guard, to dwell long beside her, and die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: My guilt is grave and I dare not beg favor. I ask only that Your Majesty pity my late mistress and permit me to register again with my original guard, to remain near her always, and die without regret."

sentences.zh: 帝憐而許之。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年復官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His office was restored in Longqing year 2.

sentences.zh: 卒贈少保，謚榮簡。

translations.literal: At death he was granted Junior Guardian, posthumous title Glorious and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was granted Junior Guardian with the temple name Glorious and Simple.

sentences.zh: 永淳公主，下嫁謝詔。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yongchun married Xie Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongchun married Xie Zhao.

sentences.zh: 睿宗二女

translations.literal: Two daughters of Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong's two daughters

sentences.zh: 長寧公主，早薨。

translations.literal: The Princess of Changning died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Changning died young.

sentences.zh: 善化公主，早薨。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shanhua died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shanhua died young.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年，

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing,
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 4,

sentences.zh: 〈（長寧、善化）〉

translations.literal: (Changning and Shanhua)〉
translations.idiomatic: Changning and Shanhua)〉

sentences.zh: 二主同日追冊。

translations.literal: the two princesses were posthumously enfeoffed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: the two princesses were posthumously enfeoffed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 世宗五女

translations.literal: Five daughters of Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's five daughters

sentences.zh: 常安公主，未下嫁。

translations.literal: The Princess of Chang'an, not yet married.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Chang'an had not yet married.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十八年薨，追冊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing she passed away and was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Jiajing year 28 and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 思柔公主，後常安主二月薨，年十二，追冊。

translations.literal: The Princess of Sirou, two months after the Princess of Chang'an passed away, aged twelve, was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Sirou died two months after the Chang'an princess, at the age of twelve, and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 寧安公主，嘉靖三十四年下嫁李和。

translations.literal: The Princess of Ning'an, in the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing married Li He.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Ning'an married Li He in Jiajing year 34.

sentences.zh: 歸善公主，嘉靖二十三年薨，追冊，葬祭視太康主。

translations.literal: The Princess of Guishan passed away in the twenty-third year of Jiajing and was posthumously enfeoffed; burial and sacrifices followed the Princess of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Guishan died in Jiajing year 23 and was posthumously enfeoffed. Her burial and sacrifices followed those of the Taikang princess.

sentences.zh: 嘉善公主，嘉靖三十六年下嫁許從誠。

translations.literal: The Princess of Jiashan, in the thirty-sixth year of Jiajing married Xu Congcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Jiashan married Xu Congcheng in Jiajing year 36.

sentences.zh: 四十三年薨。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in year 43.

sentences.zh: 穆宗六女

translations.literal: Six daughters of Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong's six daughters

sentences.zh: 蓬萊公主，早薨。

translations.literal: The Princess of Penglai died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Penglai died young.

sentences.zh: 太和公主，早薨。

translations.literal: The Princess of Taihe died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Taihe died young.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年與蓬萊主同日追冊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing she and the Princess of Penglai were posthumously enfeoffed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 she and the Penglai princess were posthumously enfeoffed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 壽陽公主，萬歷九年下嫁侯拱辰。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shouyang, in the ninth year of Wanli married Hou Gongchen.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shouyang married Hou Gongchen in Wanli year 9.

sentences.zh: 國本議起，拱辰掌宗人府，亦具疏力爭。

translations.literal: When the succession debate arose, Gongchen directed the Imperial Clan Court and also submitted a memorial arguing forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: When the debate over the heir apparent arose, Gongchen, as director of the Imperial Clan Court, submitted a forceful memorial in opposition.

sentences.zh: 卒贈太傅，謚榮康。

translations.literal: At death he was granted Grand Tutor, posthumous title Glorious and Healthy.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was granted Grand Tutor with the temple name Glorious and Healthy.

sentences.zh: 永寧公主，下嫁梁邦瑞。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yongning married Liang Bangrui.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongning married Liang Bangrui.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年薨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Wanli she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Wanli year 35.

sentences.zh: 瑞安公主，神宗同母妹。

translations.literal: The Princess of Ruian, younger sister by the same mother as Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Ruian, Shenzong's younger sister by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十三年下嫁萬煒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Wanli she married Wan Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 13 she married Wan Wei.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，主累加大長公主。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign the princess was repeatedly advanced to Grand Senior Princess.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign she was repeatedly promoted to Grand Senior Princess.

sentences.zh: 所產子及庶子長祚、弘祚皆官都督。

translations.literal: Her sons by birth and the sons by concubines Changzuo and Hongzuo all held the office of commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons and her stepsons Changzuo and Hongzuo all held the rank of commissioner.

sentences.zh: 煒官至太傅，管宗人府印。

translations.literal: Wei rose to Grand Tutor and held the seal of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Wei rose to Grand Tutor and held the seal of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 嘗以親臣侍經筵，每文華進講，佩刀入直。

translations.literal: He had served the classics lecture as an intimate minister; whenever lectures were given at Wenhua, he entered duty wearing his sword.
translations.idiomatic: He had served at the classics lecture as an intimate minister and entered Wenhua Hall for lectures wearing his sword.

sentences.zh: 李建泰西征，命煒以太牢告廟，年七十余矣。

translations.literal: When Li Jiantai marched west, Wei was ordered to announce at the temple with the great sacrifice—he was already over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiantai marched west, Wei, though already in his seventies, was ordered to announce the campaign at the ancestral temple with the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 國變，同子長祚死於賊。

translations.literal: At the dynastic collapse, he and his son Changzuo died at the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell, he and his son Changzuo were killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 弘祚投水死，長祚妻李氏亦赴井死。

translations.literal: Hongzuo threw himself into the water and died; Changzuo's wife Lady Li also went to a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo drowned himself, and Changzuo's wife Lady Li threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 延慶公主，萬歷十五年下嫁王昺。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yanqing, in the fifteenth year of Wanli married Wang Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yanqing married Wang Bing in Wanli year 15.

sentences.zh: 昺嘗救御史劉光復，觸帝怒，削職。

translations.literal: Bing had once rescued Censor Liu Guangfu, provoking the emperor's anger; his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had once rescued Censor Liu Guangfu, provoking the emperor's anger, and was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，復官。

translations.literal: When Guangzong took the throne, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne, his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 神宗十女

translations.literal: Ten daughters of Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong's ten daughters

sentences.zh: 榮昌公主，萬歷二十四年下嫁楊春元。

translations.literal: The Princess of Rongchang, in the twenty-fourth year of Wanli married Yang Chunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Rongchang married Yang Chunyuan in Wanli year 24.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，春元卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year Chunyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyuan died in year 44.

sentences.zh: 久之，主薨。

translations.literal: Long afterward the princess passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the princess died as well.

sentences.zh: 壽寧公主，二十七年下嫁冉興讓。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shouning, in the twenty-seventh year married Ran Xingrang.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shouning married Ran Xingrang in year 27.

sentences.zh: 主為神宗所愛，命五日一來朝，恩澤異他主。

translations.literal: The princess was beloved by Shenzong; he ordered her to attend court once every five days—her favors differed from other princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong favored this princess and ordered her to attend court every five days. Her privileges exceeded those of all other princesses.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，洛陽失守，莊烈帝命興讓同太監王裕民、給事中葉高標往慰福世子於河北。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign, when Luoyang fell, the Zhuanglie Emperor ordered Xingrang together with Eunuch Wang Yumin and Supervising Secretary Ye Gaobiao to go comfort the Heir of Fortune in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign, after Luoyang fell, the Zhuanglie Emperor sent Xingrang together with Eunuch Wang Yumin and Supervising Secretary Ye Gaobiao to comfort the Heir of Fortune in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 都城陷，興讓死於賊。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Xingrang died at the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Xingrang was killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 靜樂、雲和、雲夢、靈丘、仙居、泰順、香山、天臺八公主，皆早世，追冊。

translations.literal: The eight princesses of Jingle, Yunhe, Yunmeng, Lingqiu, Xianju, Taishun, Xiangshan, and Tiantai all died young and were posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The eight princesses of Jingle, Yunhe, Yunmeng, Lingqiu, Xianju, Taishun, Xiangshan, and Tiantai all died in infancy and were posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 光宗九女

translations.literal: Nine daughters of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's nine daughters

sentences.zh: 懷淑公主，七歲而薨，追冊。

translations.literal: The Princess of Huaishu passed away at seven and was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Huaishu died at the age of seven and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 餘五女皆早世，未封。

translations.literal: The remaining five daughters all died young and were not enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining five daughters all died in infancy and were never enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 寧德公主，下嫁劉有福。

translations.literal: The Princess of Ningde married Liu Youfu.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Ningde married Liu Youfu.

sentences.zh: 遂平公主，天啟七年下嫁齊贊元。

translations.literal: The Princess of Suiping, in the seventh year of Tianqi married Qi Zanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Suiping married Qi Zanyuan in Tianqi year 7.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，贊元奔南京，主前薨。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chongzhen reign Zanyuan fled to Nanjing; the princess had already passed away.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign Zanyuan fled to Nanjing; the princess had already died.

sentences.zh: 樂安公主，下嫁鞏永固。

translations.literal: The Princess of Le'an married Gong Yonggu.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Le'an married Gong Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 永固，字洪圖，宛平人，好讀書，負才氣。

translations.literal: Yonggu, style name Hongtu, was a man of Wanping; he loved reading and possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yonggu, courtesy name Hongtu, was from Wanping. He loved reading and was gifted with literary talent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年二月，帝召公、侯、伯於德政殿，言：「祖制，勛臣駙馬入監讀書，習武經弓馬。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen the emperor summoned dukes, marquises, and earls to the Hall of Virtuous Governance, saying: "By ancestral institution, meritorious ministers' sons and commandants enter the Directorate to study, learning military classics, bow, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Chongzhen year 16 the emperor summoned dukes, marquises, and earls to the Hall of Virtuous Governance and said, "By ancestral institution, the sons of meritorious ministers and commandants enter the Directorate to study the military classics and train in archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 諸臣各有子弟否？」

translations.literal: Do you ministers each have sons and younger brothers?"
translations.idiomatic: Do any of you have sons or younger brothers?"

sentences.zh: 成國公朱純臣、定國公徐允禎等皆以幼對。

translations.literal: Duke Zhu Chunchen of Cheng, Duke Xu Yunzhen of Ding, and others all answered that they were still young.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhu Chunchen of Cheng, Duke Xu Yunzhen of Ding, and others replied that their sons were still too young.

sentences.zh: 而永固獨上疏，請肄業太學。

translations.literal: Yonggu alone submitted a memorial requesting to pursue studies at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yonggu alone submitted a memorial requesting to study at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝褒答之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and answered him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him in reply.

sentences.zh: 總督趙光抃以邊事系獄，特疏申救。

translations.literal: When Governor-General Zhao Guangbian was imprisoned on border affairs, he specially memorialized to plead for his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Zhao Guangbian was imprisoned over border affairs, Yonggu submitted a special memorial pleading for his release.

sentences.zh: 又請復建文皇帝廟謚。

translations.literal: He also requested restoration of the temple and posthumous title of Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to restore the temple and posthumous title of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 事雖未行，時論韙焉。

translations.literal: Though the matters were not carried out, contemporary opinion approved them.
translations.idiomatic: Though neither proposal was adopted, contemporary opinion approved of both.

sentences.zh: 甲申春，賊破宣、大，李邦華請太子南遷，為異議所格。

translations.literal: In the spring of jiashen the rebels took Xuan and Da; Li Banghua requested the crown prince's southward relocation, but was blocked by dissenting opinion.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of jiashen year the rebels captured Xuanfu and Datong. Li Banghua urged the crown prince to relocate south, but dissenting opinion blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 及事急，帝密召永固及新樂侯劉文炳護行。

translations.literal: When matters grew urgent, the emperor secretly summoned Yonggu and Marquis Liu Wenbing of Xinle to escort the journey.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis deepened, the emperor secretly summoned Yonggu and Marquis Liu Wenbing of Xinle to escort the crown prince south.

sentences.zh: 叩頭言：「親臣不藏甲，臣等難以空手搏賊。」

translations.literal: They kowtowed and said: "Intimate ministers do not keep armor; we find it hard to fight rebels empty-handed."
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed and said, "As intimate ministers we are not permitted to keep arms. We cannot fight the rebels empty-handed."

sentences.zh: 皆相向涕泣。

translations.literal: All faced one another weeping.
translations.idiomatic: All wept facing one another.

sentences.zh: 十九日，都城陷。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 時公主已薨，未葬，永固以黃繩縛子女五人系柩旁，曰：「此帝甥也，不可汙賊手。」

translations.literal: The princess had already passed away and was not yet buried; Yonggu bound his five children with yellow cord beside the coffin, saying: "These are the emperor's kin by marriage—they must not be defiled by rebel hands."
translations.idiomatic: The princess had already died and was not yet buried. Yonggu bound his five children with yellow cord beside the coffin and said, "These are the emperor's kin by marriage. They must not fall into rebel hands."

sentences.zh: 舉劍自刎，闔室自焚死。

translations.literal: He raised his sword and cut his throat; the whole household burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: He then ran himself through with his sword, and the entire household burned themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 熹宗二女

translations.literal: Two daughters of Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong's two daughters

sentences.zh: 皆早世。

translations.literal: All died young.
translations.idiomatic: Both died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝六女

translations.literal: Six daughters of the Zhuanglie Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanglie Emperor's six daughters

sentences.zh: 坤儀公主，周皇后生。

translations.literal: The Princess of Kunyi, born to Empress Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Kunyi, daughter of Empress Zhou.

sentences.zh: 追謚。

translations.literal: Posthumous title granted.
translations.idiomatic: She was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 長平公主，年十六，帝選周顯尚主。

translations.literal: The Princess of Changping, aged sixteen; the emperor selected Zhou Xian to marry the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Changping was sixteen when the emperor chose Zhou Xian as her husband.

sentences.zh: 將婚，以寇警暫停。

translations.literal: When the wedding was imminent, it was temporarily halted on account of bandit alarms.
translations.idiomatic: The wedding was imminent but was postponed because of rebel alarms.

sentences.zh: 城陷，帝入壽寧宮，主牽帝衣哭。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the emperor entered the Palace of Longevity and Tranquility; the princess clutched his robe and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the emperor entered the Palace of Longevity and Tranquility. The princess clutched his robe and wept.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝何故生我家！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why were you born into my house!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cried, "Why were you born into this house!"

sentences.zh: 以劍揮斫之，斷左臂；

translations.literal: He swung his sword and struck her, severing her left arm;
translations.idiomatic: He swung his sword and struck her, severing her left arm.

sentences.zh: 又斫昭仁公主於昭仁殿。

translations.literal: he also struck down the Princess of Zhaoren in the Hall of Zhaoren.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck down the Princess of Zhaoren in Zhaoren Hall.

sentences.zh: 越五日，長平主復蘇。

translations.literal: Five days later the Princess of Changping revived.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the Changping princess revived.

sentences.zh: 大清順治二年上書言：「九死臣妾，蹐高天，願髡緇空王，稍申罔極。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi of the Great Qing she submitted a letter saying: "Nine-deaths subject and concubine, treading the high heaven, I wish to shave my head and enter the empty king's realm, slightly to express boundless grief."
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 2 of the Great Qing she submitted a letter: "I am a subject who has survived nine deaths, yet I still tread beneath heaven's height. I wish to shave my head and enter the Buddhist order, that I may in some small measure express my boundless grief."

sentences.zh: 詔不許，命顯復尚故主，土田邸第金錢車馬錫予有加。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it; Xian was ordered again to marry the former princess; fields, residences, money, carriages, and horses were bestowed with additions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused her request and ordered Xian to marry her again. Fields, residences, money, carriages, and horses were bestowed upon them in abundance.

sentences.zh: 主涕泣。

translations.literal: The princess wept with tears.
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 逾年病卒。

translations.literal: More than a year later she died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later she died of illness.

sentences.zh: 賜葬廣寧門外。
